verdict.rationale: GitBook's own docs say OpenAPI-based reference pages let users test endpoints right on the page with interactive blocks, and the pricing page lists interactive API playgrounds as a feature. That is the embedded try-it playground this story asks for. missing for 10: in-depth documentation of how live calls are executed (authentication handling, request configuration, proxying), independent or hands-on corroboration that real API calls succeed from the playground.

support.subject: As a developer, readers can try real API calls from an interactive playground embedded in the reference docs

citations.quote: let your users test endpoints right on the page with interactive blocks
